target.title: test(qa): prove native command targeting across QA transports
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `native-command-session-target` QA scenario linked a harness-heavy Vitest file, so its primary maturity evidence did not prove that a native channel command could interrupt a real active routed conversation through QA Lab. The first version of this PR moved that behavior into a QA flow, but still restricted it to the synthetic QA Channel transport.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the linked test with one transport-portable QA flow using the shared `QaTransportAdapter` native-command action:

- QA Channel preserves its native-command metadata path.
- Crabline Telegram now injects a real Telegram `bot_command` entity through `@openclaw/crabline@0.1.7`.
- The taxonomy `smoke-ci` profile selects Crabline Telegram, while the default QA suite can still run the same scenario through QA Channel.
- The isolated flow waits for an active routed session, sends native `/stop`, verifies the abort acknowledgement, and proves the conversation accepts a recovery turn.

The superseded native-stop E2E case remains removed. No taxonomy or coverage IDs are added.

Dependency work: openclaw/crabline#35 added provider-faithful Telegram native-command ingress and shipped as `v0.1.7`.

## User Impact

QA maturity evidence now gives honest primary coverage for the existing `channels.native-command-session-target` ID in `smoke-ci`. `channels.native-commands` remains secondary coverage. The same YAML behavior remains runnable through QA Channel for local debugging.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-planning.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-flow-runner.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-runtime-api.test.ts extensions/qa-channel/src/inbound.test.ts extensions/qa-channel/src/gateway.test.ts src/channels/native-command-session-targets.test.ts`
  - 8 files, 86 tests passed against installed `@openclaw/crabline@0.1.7`.
- QA Channel scenario:
  - `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario native-command-session-target --concurrency 1 --fast ...`
  - Passed: native `/stop` aborted the active run and the recovery turn returned `QA-NATIVE-STOP-RECOVERY-OK`.
- Taxonomy `smoke-ci` / Crabline Telegram scenario:
  - `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 node scripts/run-node.mjs qa run --qa-profile smoke-ci --category channel-framework.channel-actions-commands-and-approvals --scenario native-command-session-target --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1 ...`
  - Passed and emitted `channels.native-command-session-target` as primary evidence.
- Crabline `v0.1.7` release:
  - Release run: https://github.com/openclaw/crabline/actions/runs/28548996639
  - npm publication verified as `@openclaw/crabline@0.1.7`.
- Testbox-through-Crabbox `pnpm check:changed`:
  - Provider: `blacksmith-testbox`
  - ID: `tbx_01kwfsp723wxxdr7pb9xt7m1b7`
  - Passed typecheck, lint, import-cycle checks, dependency/lock guards, and repository guards.
  - Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28549264406
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output ...`
  - Clean: no accepted/actionable findings; confidence 0.91.
